summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder, was admitted due to darker red output from his bilateral nephrostomy tubes and absent drainage from the right tube. He had no pain or fever. He was recently discharged after treatment for urosepsis and was continuing oral ciprofloxacin. Imaging and nephrostogram revealed a clogged right tube and bleeding from the left nephrostomy tract. Both tubes were replaced, with the left upsized to improve drainage and reduce bleeding. He was observed overnight, remained stable, and his hemoglobin showed an expected post-procedure drop. He was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, monitor tube output, and complete a CBC in one week. Wound care for existing pressure ulcers was emphasized.
